phase: Phase 1a — migration 022 applied to Pilot. Record-only payment management; no fund movement of any kind.

production_untouched.note: A grep for 'Claude-Session' on main returns 117 — all from earlier work merged long before this session. A grep for THIS session id returns 0, and none of this session's six commits is an ancestor of main.

fidelity._why: The migration was transcribed into the API rather than piped from disk, so 'what is deployed is what was reviewed' had to be measured, not assumed. Each deployed function body (pg_proc.prosrc) was whitespace-normalised and hashed against the same body extracted from the file.

drift_found_and_corrected.difference: one in-body comment line was dropped in transcription: '-- Recomputed inside this transaction from the actual non-voided rows.'
drift_found_and_corrected.functional_impact: none — the executable statements were identical
drift_found_and_corrected.action: the function was re-applied verbatim from the file so the deployed object is byte-identical to the approved one

fidelity.false_alarm_noted: A first comparison reported all 14 differing. That was the verification query, not the deployment: Postgres btrim() with one argument strips spaces but NOT newlines, so its normalised string kept a leading space that JavaScript's trim() removed. Corrected to btrim(regexp_replace(...)) which matches.

resync_proc_md5.note: expected: 022 replaces it to add the payments retention clause
